sources.evidence_text: The effective federal funds rate was reported at 3.88 percent on each trading day from November 13 through November 19.
sources.why_it_matters: Stable overnight rates confirm that policy implementation remained unchanged, though they do not by themselves show whether future cuts were priced out.

sources.title: The Economic Outlook and Some Thoughts on Labor Market Dynamism
sources.evidence_text: Waller said economic growth is strong, employment is near its long-run rate, inflation remains too high, and further tightening will be needed relatively soon.
sources.why_it_matters: With employment near maximum and inflation above target, this reaction-function assessment directly supports fewer cuts and possible additional tightening.

sources.title: The U.S. Economy in Global Context
sources.evidence_text: Cook said inflation had stayed above 3 percent for much of the year with little evidence of decline, while unemployment was 4.1 percent and hiring remained modest but consistent.
sources.why_it_matters: Low unemployment reduces the urgency to support employment, leaving persistent inflation as the dominant reason to keep policy restrictive.

sources.title: Monetary Policy amid Frequent and Complex Shocks
sources.evidence_text: Vice Chair Jefferson said policymakers must assess shocks against both employment and price-stability objectives and may prioritize employment risks when price pressures are contained.
sources.why_it_matters: The conditional framework leaves policy dependent on whether incoming data show greater inflation or employment risks.

sources.title: Treasury yields jump as stock futures rebound
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield rose above 4.69%, and CME FedWatch pricing implied about a 98% chance of a 25-basis-point December hike.
sources.why_it_matters: Higher front-end yields and elevated hike odds signal that markets have priced out easing and assigned a high probability to tightening.

sources.title: Fed minutes: Officials favored holding rates steady in October, but they see hikes ahead
sources.evidence_text: The October FOMC minutes indicated that almost all participants viewed additional rate increases as likely appropriate under their baseline inflation and labor-market outlooks.
sources.why_it_matters: Broad agreement among policymakers that hikes may be needed shows the committee’s baseline reaction function is oriented toward further restraint.

sources.title: Treasury yields move sharply lower as investors flee to safe havens
sources.evidence_text: Despite a decline in the 2-year yield to about 4.63%, futures still implied approximately a 92% probability of a quarter-point December hike.
sources.why_it_matters: The lower 2-year yield weakens the market signal modestly, but persistent high hike odds still point clearly away from an easing regime.

sources.title: Daily Treasury Rates — November 2026 CSV
sources.evidence_text: The two-year Treasury yield was 4.76% on November 19 before falling to 4.63% on November 20, showing substantial but volatile front-end pricing.
sources.why_it_matters: Volatile two-year yields signal uncertainty, but levels well above typical easing-regime pricing point to a restrictive expected policy stance.

sources.title: State Employment and Unemployment — October 2026
sources.evidence_text: The national unemployment rate remained 4.1%; unemployment rates declined in three states and the District of Columbia, increased in one state, and were unchanged in 46 states.
sources.why_it_matters: Broadly stable state labor-market conditions provide little evidence of either rapid deterioration requiring cuts or widespread overheating requiring tightening.

sources.title: Payroll employment increased by 885,000 from October 2025 to October 2026
sources.evidence_text: Payroll employment rose by 885,000 over the year through October 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Positive year-over-year employment growth supports a view that labor-market conditions do not yet require faster easing.

sources.title: Involuntary part-time employment rose by 339,000 to 4.8 million in October 2026
sources.evidence_text: The number of workers employed part time for economic reasons increased by 339,000 to 4.8 million in October 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Rising involuntary part-time work signals underutilized labor and provides some support for further policy easing.

sources.title: Job openings rate little changed at 4.5 percent in September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The job openings rate was little changed at 4.5 percent in September 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Stable vacancies suggest labor demand is cooling only gradually, leaving the reaction-function signal balanced.

sources.title: Real average hourly earnings unchanged in October 2026
sources.evidence_text: Real average hourly earnings for all employees were unchanged in October 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Stagnant real pay growth limits evidence of demand-driven wage pressure and modestly supports continued easing.

sources.title: Daily Treasury Outlook
sources.evidence_text: An upside inflation surprise drove a sharp repricing toward more aggressive Fed hikes, with the 2-year Treasury yield rising about 18 basis points to 4.731% and a small probability of a 50-basis-point December move emerging.
sources.why_it_matters: A renewed inflation shock raises the policy rate required to restore price stability and makes further easing less likely.

sources.title: U.S. 2-Year Treasury Auction Shows Solid Demand
sources.evidence_text: The Treasury sold $69 billion of 2-year notes at a 4.700% high yield, just below the 4.703% when-issued yield, with the 2-year yield near 4.696% afterward.
sources.why_it_matters: Solid auction demand limits the signal from elevated yields, leaving this event broadly neutral for the Fed reaction function.

sources.title: State Employment and Unemployment Summary - October 2026
sources.evidence_text: The national unemployment rate remained 4.1 percent, with rates lower in three states and the District of Columbia, higher in one state, and unchanged in 46 states.
sources.why_it_matters: Broadly stable state-level labor-market conditions indicate neither a sharp deterioration requiring faster cuts nor an overheating signal requiring tightening.

sources.title: Beige Book - October 2026
sources.evidence_text: District contacts reported modest overall wage growth, with isolated higher premiums for highly skilled workers and some additional cost-of-living and benefit-cost pressures.
sources.why_it_matters: Moderate aggregate wage growth reduces immediate overheating pressure, while pockets of wage acceleration leave the Fed cautious about service inflation.

sources.title: Fed officials divided over need for larger interest rate hikes in December
sources.evidence_text: October headline and core CPI increased 0.4% and 0.3% month over month, respectively, with inflation exceeding expectations for a third consecutive month.
sources.why_it_matters: Repeated upside inflation surprises imply persistent price pressure and argue for fewer cuts or additional tightening.

sources.title: Fed Watches Inflation Picture Turn Uglier
sources.evidence_text: The article reported that federal-funds futures implied a 100% probability of a December rate hike as of November 18, including a 9.6% probability of a 50-basis-point increase.
sources.why_it_matters: Complete pricing of a hike indicates markets had moved decisively from an easing regime toward policy tightening.

sources.title: Fed has 'work to do' to lower inflation, Williams says
sources.evidence_text: New York Fed President Williams said persistently high inflation continued to point toward tighter monetary policy and projected inflation would remain above target into 2027.
sources.why_it_matters: A senior policymaker’s above-target inflation outlook supports maintaining restrictive policy rather than resuming rate cuts.

sources.title: Fed 50 bp December hike bets fade as pause odds emerge
sources.evidence_text: The report said markets still favored a 25-basis-point December hike, while the probability of a larger hike fell to zero and the probability of a pause rose to about 12%.
sources.why_it_matters: Pricing still leans toward tightening, but fading odds of a larger move indicate some moderation in the drift away from easing.

sources.title: Treasuries-US yields slip as AI rally fizzles
sources.evidence_text: CME FedWatch showed markets fully pricing at least a 25-basis-point December rate hike, with a 4.4% probability of a 50-basis-point hike, while the 2-year Treasury yield was 4.662%.
sources.why_it_matters: A fully priced near-term hike indicates markets expect policy to move away from easing and toward active tightening.

sources.title: Federal Reserve officials divided over need for larger interest rate hikes in December
sources.evidence_text: The report said CME FedWatch pricing implied nearly certain tightening in December, with substantial probabilities of further hikes in January and March 2027.
sources.why_it_matters: Market pricing indicates that traders expect the Fed to continue raising rates rather than resume cuts.

sources.title: Almost all Fed policymakers saw further interest rate hikes as likely
sources.evidence_text: The report summarized the October minutes as showing that almost all participants viewed additional rate increases as likely appropriate to bring inflation back under control.
sources.why_it_matters: Broad agreement that further hikes may be needed indicates a strong anti-inflationary reaction function and little support for near-term cuts.

sources.title: Treasuries-US yields climb as Nvidia reinstates Huang
sources.evidence_text: The report said markets were almost completely pricing at least a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December, while the two-year yield rose sharply during the session.
sources.why_it_matters: Near-complete pricing of a forthcoming hike strongly signals that markets view the next policy move as tightening rather than easing.

sources.title: Monthly Fixed Income Market Outlook
sources.evidence_text: Hong Leong Bank reported that hotter October inflation and hawkish Federal Reserve commentary pushed yields higher and forecast additional quarter-point rate increases.
sources.why_it_matters: The scenario links inflation and official communication to a projected continuation of tightening, though it is not an official forecast.

sources.title: October 2026 Bond Market Comments
sources.evidence_text: Baird said the two-year Treasury yield fell about 30 basis points in October while the FOMC maintained its policy-rate range after a divided vote.
sources.why_it_matters: The monthly decline in the policy-sensitive two-year yield points toward easing, but the split decision and unchanged policy make the overall signal mixed.
